technical.lead: White House FMRB executive order draft circulates to interagency review
technical.body: Senior White House officials circulate an interagency draft executive order proposing a Frontier Model Review Board (FMRB) co-chaired by NIST and the ODNI cyber lead, with mandatory pre-release notification 30 days before any model surpassing offensive-cyber thresholds mapped to AISI's 32-step "The Last Ones" range — thresholds that GPT-5.5 + Mythos already breached in the May 1 evaluation. The draft leans on Defense Production Act §708 voluntary information-sharing authority rather than new statutory rulemaking, sidestepping APA notice-and-comment; AI Policy Institute, R Street, and AI Now have flagged the lack of a public-comment window as a litigation vector. The same-day EU AI Office + UK AISI joint memorandum on cyber-evaluation reciprocity (an AISI TLO-range run satisfies AI Act §51 systemic-risk pre-deployment requirements when conducted within 90 days of EU placement, with Mistral, Aleph Alpha, Anthropic, and OpenAI as the initial cohort) defines the trans-Atlantic pair to the FMRB shape. The third leg lands in the UK: NCSC formally extends the NHS open-source repository wall-off advisory to DWP, HMRC, and Network Rail with a rolling May 15 deadline while HM Treasury pauses public-sector LLM-coding-assistant procurements pending supply-chain review.

technical.lead: Cerebras prices IPO at 128 dollars, top of range, 27 billion valuation
technical.body: Cerebras Systems prices its initial public offering at $128 per share — $3 above the upper end of the previously disclosed $115-$125 range — raising approximately $3.58B at a fully-diluted market cap of ~$27.2B. Underwriters Citi, Goldman Sachs, and Morgan Stanley exercise the green-shoe in full, lifting total proceeds to ~$4.12B and making this the largest US tech IPO year-to-date 2026 by both raise size and pricing-vs-range outperformance. OpenAI's $1B warrant package (covering ~33M shares, ~12% of float, struck at the Series H reference) prices in-the-money on listing; Cerebras shares open Thursday under ticker CBRS on Nasdaq. The print-day proof that the AI-accelerator-IPO template is open immediately accelerates the second-tier inference-chip cohort: SambaNova and Groq are reported to be moving S-1 confidential submissions to within 60-90 days, while Tenstorrent is in late-stage discussions with Hyundai and Samsung Foundry on an IPO bridge round at >$3B. The +2.4% pricing-above-range margin sets a floor for the structured-warrant + frontier-lab supply-contract IPO shape.

technical.lead: CISA adds n8n RCE to KEV catalog as LangGraph + LiteLLM CVEs land
technical.body: CISA adds n8n CVE-2026-21858 (Ni8mare, CVSS 10.0) to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with a federal-civilian-executive-branch remediation deadline of May 21 — the first agentic-AI-workflow-platform CVE to enter the KEV. Shadowserver's first-week scan finds ~14,200 internet-exposed n8n instances pre-1.121.0 globally (US 4,610 / DE 1,920 / IN 1,455 / FR 880 / JP 720), of which ~62% remain unpatched seven days post-disclosure; Censys and Orca confirm in-the-wild exploitation against Telegram, Discord, and GitHub webhook entry points. Within the same 24-hour window two more high-severity agentic-platform CVEs land: LangChain LangGraph CVE-2026-44012 (CVSS 9.1, SSRF in the checkpoint-replay endpoint allowing pivot to cloud-metadata services) and LiteLLM CVE-2026-44188 (CVSS 8.8, authentication bypass in the proxy admin API). Sysdig Threat Research observed exploitation attempts against honeypots within 18 hours of disclosure for both. Separately, joint Adversa AI / Wiz / Sysdig telemetry places exposed MCP servers at ~9,400 (up from ~7,000 four weeks prior, +34%), with ~58% still operating with no authorization controls; Microsoft Defender for Cloud announces GA of an MCP-server threat-detection module the same day.

technical.lead: Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 + OpenAI agent registry land same day
technical.body: Anthropic ships Claude Code 3.0 with three structural changes: a sandboxed-skill registry that signs and version-pins shareable agent skills (a vendor-provided governance answer to the agent-skill attack-surface concern); per-tenant Mythos Preview gating tied to AISI cyber-evaluation results, so enterprise customers must opt-in via a contractual ethics-and-misuse rider before Mythos-class capabilities are exposed (the first contractual implementation of the Project Glasswing model); and native sub-agent dispatch with token-budget bookkeeping, GA across Mac, Linux, Windows plus a new VS Code extension. OpenAI graduates its May 1 Codex CLI /goal feature into a richer /agent command with explicit Plan-Apply two-phase execution, while ChatGPT Enterprise announces GA of a per-org agent registry with FedRAMP-Moderate authorization and SOC-2 Type II report scope expansion to cover the registry plus audit ledger. Both same-day landings answer the agentic-AI-attack-surface concern raised by the n8n KEV addition with vendor-provided control planes. In parallel Mistral publishes one-week-post-preview Workflows go-lives at Capgemini, Atos, and EDF, with paid tenancy now exceeding 240 enterprise customers (up from ~60 at preview) and daily-execution count surpassing 3.4M (vs ~800K).

technical.lead: Unsloth ships router-only LoRA for MoE fine-tuning on Qwen3.6-Max
technical.body: Unsloth announces native fine-tuning support for Qwen3.6-Max — the open-weight competitor to GPT-5.5 from the April 15 Qwen drop — including 4-bit and 8-bit dynamic-bits-per-parameter QLoRA on a single H100 (80GB) instance, plus a new LoRA-on-MoE-router-only training mode that targets only the router weights of mixture-of-experts models. Per Unsloth's benchmarks, router-only fine-tuning on Qwen3.6-Max achieves 73% of full-LoRA-on-experts task accuracy at 8.4% of training-step time and 12% of peak VRAM, a structurally new compute envelope for MoE fine-tuning. The joint Hugging Face engineering pipeline now extends the 1.8-3.3x faster BERT/embedding/classifier path to long-context-RL-tuned router-only adapters; full fine-tunes still export to GGUF. On the inference side, vLLM ships v0.11 with a RadixAttention-compatible prefix-cache that closes the H100 throughput gap to SGLang from 29% to 14% (~14,200 tok/s vs ~16,200 tok/s on the same shared-prefix workload per the Yotta Labs benchmark refresh); Cloudflare Infire continues to lead at the edge with prefill/decode disaggregation. Together these are the local-LLM training-stack and serving-stack Pareto frontier movements of the week.
